published_by: Ofgem, Annex 9 to the Default Tariff Cap decision -- the published breakdown of policy costs in a domestic bill
what_this_is: WHAT A SUPPLIER PAYS FOR THE CAPACITY MARKET, PER MWh SUPPLIED. This is a LEVY ON DEMAND and it is a completely different quantity from the clearing price in `capacity_market_auction_results.json`, which is what a capacity PROVIDER is paid per kW of de-rated capacity it has an agreement for. The two are related only through a settlement the Settlement Body performs and neither this file nor that one publishes: the total cost of all capacity agreements, recovered from all suppliers in proportion to their demand in the winter peak periods.

basis.year_key: the calendar year the Apr-Mar obligation year OPENS in, so 2023 is obligation year 2023/24 -- the same convention as the Renewables Obligation, and NOT the Oct-Sep CM delivery year the auction record is keyed by
basis.derivation: ANNEX 9 DOES NOT PUBLISH A PER-YEAR FIGURE, and saying it did is what cost a BLOCKING finding on 2026-09-07. It publishes an ANNUALISED GBP-per-customer-per-year level IN FORCE DURING EACH CAP PERIOD -- six-month periods to Sep 2022, quarterly after. `annex9_cap_periods` below holds those rows verbatim. An obligation year's figure is the DURATION-WEIGHTED MEAN of the cap-period levels overlapping Apr-Mar (weights are `months`, so 2022/23 is 6/3/3 and not a plain average), and `gbp_per_mwh` is that mean divided by `benchmark_mwh` and rounded to 2dp. THE DIVISION IS ON THE UNROUNDED MEAN: 2018/19 is 11.364754/3.1 = 3.6661 -> 3.67, whereas the rounded 11.36/3.1 = 3.66. Running the derivation against a rounded per-customer figure reproduces eight of nine rows and fails at 2018, which is exactly the false defect this wording now prevents.
basis.segments: ALL of them. Domestic, SME and I&C pay the same GBP/MWh -- there is no domestic exemption, unlike CCL
basis.payment_method: NOT differentiated. The CM row is identical across the Other Payment Method and Standard Credit tables in sheet 1b, asserted cell-by-cell across all 28 cap periods when this file was rebuilt rather than assumed. The single-rate electricity table is the one read; gas carries no CM row (it is zero throughout).

there_is_no_de_rating_here: AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS FILE EXISTING SEPARATELY. De-rating is a haircut applied to a capacity PROVIDER's connection capacity to reflect how much of it can be relied on at a system stress event. A supplier's obligation is a payment scaled by the electricity it SUPPLIED. Demand is not de-rated -- there is no published factor for it, because the concept does not apply. `company/regulatory/capacity_market.py` carried `_DERATING_FACTOR = 0.92  # Assumed average de-rated supply margin %` and applied it to a supplier obligation; it was invented, it was the wrong concept, and removing it made that module's answer WORSE against this series, which is how we learned it was propping up a route that was wrong for a different reason.
the_clearing_price_is_not_this_number: A supplier levy derived by multiplying a clearing price by an estimated peak demand does not reproduce this series in level or even in the sign of its error. Measured 2026-09-07 against the route this file replaced: 8.51x at 2016, 0.21x at 2020, 0.03x at 2021, 4.21x at 2022, 1.69x at 2024. The auction clearing price is an input to a settlement, not a proxy for its output.

provenance_legend.primary: every overlapping Annex 9 cap period was read from the workbook and the obligation year is fully covered (`months_published` == 12). These rows are asserted by the derivation control.
provenance_legend.estimated: outside Annex 9's coverage and derived, with the derivation stated in the row's note. Carries a null `gbp_per_customer_year` and is EXCLUDED from the derivation control -- the control asserts that the excluded set is exactly the `estimated` rows, so a primary row cannot escape the check by nulling its per-customer figure.

source.workbook: Ofgem Annex 9 'Levelisation allowance methodology and levelised cap levels' v1.11, sheet '1b Historical level tables', row 'CM' of the Typical-consumption table, Electricity Single-Rate Metering Arrangement
source.supersedes: v1.8 (November 2025), via docs/market_research/capacity_market_levy_2016_2024.md, which is what this artefact was built from at version 1. v1.11 extends the record by the whole of 2024/25 H2 and 2025/26, which is what made the 2024 correction and the 2025 row possible.

levy_gbp_per_mwh.note: TA auctions only; T-4 delivery had not started and Annex 9's historical table begins Apr 2017. No cap-period rows exist for this year, so it carries no per-customer figure and is EXCLUDED from the derivation control.
TA (GBP27.50/kW) + Early Auction (GBP6.95/kW) only. Two six-month cap periods.

First full T-4 delivery year (T-4 at GBP19.40/kW). THIS ROW WAS FILED AS A DEFECT ON 2026-09-07 AND WAS NOT ONE: 11.36/3.1 = 3.66, but the unrounded 11.364754/3.1 = 3.6661 -> 3.67. The old note carried the ROUNDED per-customer figure and the derivation was run against it, so the row appeared to contradict itself. Double rounding, not a transcription.
T-4 at GBP18.00/kW; T-1 at GBP0.77/kW.
T-4 at GBP22.50/kW. Highest per-customer level of the six-month-cap era.
Cheapest year -- the 2017 T-4 cleared at only GBP8.40/kW.

NOTE THE DIRECTION: the T-1 for this delivery year cleared at the GBP75/kW CAP and the levy still FELL, because the volume behind that price was small and the suspended T-4's replacement T-3 was cheap. A levy modelled off a clearing price gets this year backwards. Mixed period lengths: one six-month cap period then two quarterly ones, so the mean is DURATION-WEIGHTED (6/3/3), not a plain average.
T-4 at GBP15.97/kW + T-1 at GBP60/kW. Four quarterly cap periods.

CORRECTED 2026-09-07 FROM 7.27 TO 6.99. The 7.27 was Apr-Sep 2024 ONLY -- the artefact said so ('H1 ONLY ... the least settled figure here') and it was the honest reading of Annex 9 v1.8. v1.11 publishes all four quarters, and the H2 level (20.798362) is materially below H1 (23.470326, 21.613732), so the half-year figure OVERSTATED the year by 4.0%.
NEWLY ESTABLISHED 2026-09-07. Annex 9 v1.8 did not carry this year and the artefact recorded it as not established; v1.11 publishes all four quarters of Apr 2025 - Mar 2026.

what_is_not_established: 2026/27 ONWARDS, AND THE RULE IS ENFORCED RATHER THAN PROMISED. v1.11 publishes Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep and Oct-Dec 2026 (9 of 12 months) and those three cap periods ARE carried in `annex9_cap_periods` -- this file holds the publisher's rows verbatim, including ones no levy row is derived from. Jan-Mar 2027 is not yet set, so 2026/27 cannot be duration-weighted and gets NO row in `levy_gbp_per_mwh`: a 9-month mean would be a real-looking number for a year nobody has published. The derivation control asserts BOTH halves of that -- every obligation year with 12 months of cap periods HAS a levy row, and every year with fewer has none -- so the partial year cannot be quietly promoted and a completed year cannot be quietly forgotten. There is no extrapolation and no carry-forward here: a caller asking for a year outside this record gets None. THIS CLAUSE PREVIOUSLY SAID '2025/26 onwards ... Annex 9 has not published it', which was true of v1.8 and false of v1.11; a not-established claim in the commons is itself a dated reading and rots exactly like a figure.

source_check.how_to_recheck: GET the Ofgem default tariff cap landing page https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/energy-policy-and-regulation/policy-and-regulatory-programmes/default-tariff-cap and read the version in the Annex 9 filename it links. If it is above v1.11, a later cap period has been published and the LAST obligation year in `levy_gbp_per_mwh` may have been derived from a partial year -- which is exactly how the 2024/25 row came to be 4.0% wrong.
